newsitem.title: JAPAN: Harsh bank penalties needed to gain trust - Kajiyama.
newsitem.headline: Harsh bank penalties needed to gain trust - Kajiyama.

text.p: Harsh penalties for violations of Japan's banking laws are needed to maintain public trust, Japan's Chief Cabinet Secretary Seiroku Kajiyama told a parliamentary committee meeting on Tuesday.
He added that stiff penalties can also help unearth wrongdoing.
Current banking laws have been effective, he said, but the government must also consider how to penalise banking industry ties with corporate racketeers, he said.
Kajiyama said Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd's (DKB) alleged links with racketeers are widely believed by the Japanese public to have involved the whole bank, not just individual bankers.

"Although it is not good to base things just on imagination, the general public deeply suspects top bank officials were involved in this problem at DKB. They do not think that an individual banker did something bad and the top officials were trying to supress it," he said.
"I feel that these criminal acts should not be pardoned," he added.
